note: Editor-side claims. A public draft may quote only a publicQuote whose wordCount is 25 or less. editorExcerpt stays in this file. Rank in serp-evidence.json is not authority.

claims.statement: On 2026-10-12 the Stardew Valley Wiki front page version table listed the computer, PS4, and Xbox One versions as 1.6.15, updated December 20, 2024. The same date and version string appeared on rows whose links point at Console Version History for Switch and Mobile Version History for iOS and Android.
claims.versionCondition: Front-page labels read on this date. This is not a patch-note audit of every platform build.
claims.publicQuote: 1.6.15 (Updated December 20, 2024)
claims.limit: The printed HTML window showed the words Computer version, PS4 version, and Xbox One version beside that string. Switch, iOS, and Android were identified from the history anchors on those rows, not from a second full reading of their label text.

claims.statement: The same front-page table listed a PlayStation Vita row as 1.02, updated June 20, 2018.
claims.versionCondition: Vita version label on the front page. The Vita version-history section was not opened.
claims.publicQuote: 1.02 (Updated June 20, 2018)
claims.limit: Do not treat the 1.6 Iridium Scythe as available on the Vita version this table lists. No Vita patch note was opened.

claims.statement: The Scythe is a starter tool. It cuts grass, weeds, young trees, and moss, uses no energy, and is required for harvesting certain crops. The page's examples are Amaranth, Kale, and Wheat. One scythe starts in inventory. It can also be used as a weak weapon.
claims.versionCondition: Current Scythe page. The 1.6 history line is claim F05.
claims.publicQuote: It is also required for harvesting certain crops (i.e., Amaranth, Kale, Wheat).
claims.limit: The i.e. list is examples. It is not a closed list. See F15.

claims.statement: The Scythe cannot be upgraded at the Blacksmith. The Golden Scythe is found from the statue in the Quarry Mine. The Iridium Scythe is received after Farming Mastery.
claims.versionCondition: Current Scythe page. Golden and Iridium introduction versions are F07 and F08.
claims.publicQuote: The Scythe cannot be upgraded at the Blacksmith, but better scythes may be found.
claims.limit: Farming Mastery is not Farming level 10 by itself. See F33.

claims.statement: The Scythe history says that in 1.6 it can no longer be lost from inventory when the player dies. The Golden Scythe history has the same 1.6 line.
claims.versionCondition: Wiki history attribute for 1.6. The original 1.6 launch post was not opened.
claims.publicQuote: Can no longer lose from inventory when dying.
claims.limit: Second source for the Golden Scythe line: https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Golden_Scythe oldid 191051.

claims.statement: With a silo, cutting farm grass with the basic Scythe has a 50 percent chance to add one hay, or two hay from Blue Grass. The Golden Scythe page says 75 percent hay per swipe, up from 50 percent. The Iridium Scythe page says 100 percent hay per swipe, up from 75 percent.
claims.versionCondition: Current tool pages. Hay citations on the Golden and Iridium pages point at game code, which was not re-executed.
claims.publicQuote: 75% chance per swipe to harvest hay from grass, up from 50%.
claims.limit: This is hay from grass, not Wheat's separate 40 percent hay drop in F12. Golden oldid 191051. Iridium oldid 186836.

claims.statement: The Golden Scythe's listed benefits are a larger radius than the basic Scythe, a higher chance to cut all grass in that radius, 75 percent hay, and 13 damage instead of 1-3. The benefit list does not say it harvests ordinary crops. History says it was introduced in 1.4.
claims.versionCondition: Introduced in 1.4 per the Golden Scythe history.
claims.publicQuote: It's more powerful than a normal scythe.
claims.limit: Do not claim it destroys Parsnips, and do not claim it harvests hand-picked crops. The page does not say either.

claims.statement: The Iridium Scythe is obtained after claiming Farming Mastery. Its item text says it can harvest any crops and is excellent at gathering hay. Its benefit list says it can harvest items grown on tilled soil within its swing range, including regular crops, crops in Garden Pots, Spring Onions, and forageables grown from Wild Seeds. It also has a larger radius than the Golden Scythe, is more likely to cut all grass, gives 100 percent hay per swipe, and inflicts 20 damage instead of 13. History says it was introduced in 1.6.
claims.versionCondition: Introduced in 1.6 per this page. Outside the Vita 1.02 label in F02. Radius, hay, and damage citations point at game files and were not re-executed.
claims.publicQuote: Can be used to harvest any crops.
claims.editorExcerpt: Can harvest items grown on tilled soil within its swing range, including regular crops, those grown in Garden Pots, Spring Onions, and other forageables grown from Wild Seeds.
claims.limit: The benefit list does not name Fiber Seeds. Do not add Fiber to this sentence. Farming Mastery requirements are F33.

claims.statement: The Iridium Scythe wiki history for 1.6.9 says harvesting crops grown from Wild Seeds was fixed so they no longer always produced normal quality and gave no XP or Mastery. The official 1.6.9 changelog on stardewvalley.net, read the same day, has separate lines: Gatherer can double harvested forage when using an iridium scythe; forage crops from garden pots no longer always being low quality with no XP; an iridium scythe on forage crops now gives XP and the forage level quality boost; Junimo harvesters no longer lose item color when a full hut drops a crop on the ground. These wordings stay side by side.
claims.versionCondition: 1.6.9 changelog page. Wiki counterpart is Iridium Scythe oldid 186836, history line 1.6.9.
claims.publicQuote: With the Gatherer skill, the chance to double harvested forage now applies when using an iridium scythe too.
claims.limit: Do not merge the wiki Wild Seed sentence and the official forage or garden-pot sentences into one claim. The 1.6 launch post that introduced the tool was not opened.

claims.statement: Kale grows in Spring after 6 days and is harvested using a Scythe or better. The page lists 17 Farming XP.
claims.versionCondition: Current Kale page. The words or better are this page's words. The page does not name Golden or Iridium in that sentence.
claims.publicQuote: Kale is harvested using a Scythe or better.
claims.limit: XP is recorded only as the page's harvest line. Do not turn this article into an XP guide.

claims.statement: Amaranth grows in Fall after 7 days and is harvested using a Scythe or better. The page lists 21 Farming XP.
claims.versionCondition: Current Amaranth page.
claims.publicQuote: Amaranth is harvested using a Scythe or better.
claims.limit: Same limit as F10 on the words or better.

claims.statement: Wheat grows in Summer or Fall after 4 days and is harvested using a Scythe or better. Any scythe harvest has a 40 percent chance to also drop hay. A Wheat plant of any growth stage that is in the ground on Summer 28 continues on Fall 1, and fertilizer under it remains. Fully grown Wheat may be left until Fall 1 to keep fertilizer and tilled soil. The page lists 6 Farming XP.
claims.versionCondition: Hay-on-harvest was added in 1.4 per this page's history. The 40 percent citation points at Crop::harvest and was not re-executed.
claims.publicQuote: Wheat is harvested using a Scythe or better.
claims.editorExcerpt: Wheat has a 40% chance to also drop hay when harvested with any Scythe.
claims.limit: Leaving Wheat until Fall 1 keeps soil and fertilizer. That is a different goal from harvesting it during Summer.

claims.statement: Unmilled Rice grows from Rice Shoots in Spring and is harvested using a Scythe. That sentence does not say or better. Most tiles take 8 days. Shoots about within 3 tiles of water are irrigated, mature in 6 days, and do not need watering.
claims.versionCondition: History says introduced in 1.4. Extra-yield odds on the same page are excluded from this how-to.
claims.publicQuote: Unmilled Rice is harvested using a Scythe.
claims.limit: Do not copy or better from Kale onto this sentence. Iridium's separate regular-crop rule is F08.

claims.statement: Fiber Seeds say to harvest with the scythe. They take 7 days, grow in any season including Winter, need no daily watering, and still need tilled soil. Each plant drops 4 to 7 Fiber, with a 10 percent chance of one Mixed Seeds. The page says they are not considered Crops, but Junimos still harvest them in range of a Junimo Hut. History says introduced in 1.5.
claims.versionCondition: Introduced in 1.5. A 1.6 history line only fixes Farm Computer counting them as unwatered.
claims.publicQuote: Harvest with the scythe.
claims.limit: F08 does not name Fiber Seeds. Do not claim the Iridium Scythe specifically harvests them.

claims.statement: Scythe-required pages opened on 2026-10-12 are Kale, Amaranth, Wheat, Unmilled Rice, and Fiber Seeds, plus the Scythe page examples Amaranth, Kale, and Wheat. This set is the pages read, not a proof that no other crop uses a scythe.
claims.versionCondition: Current English wiki pages opened this date.
claims.limit: A full-text search was not repeated in this continuation. Do not call the list exhaustive.

claims.statement: On PC, left-click or C is Use tool or place item. Right-click or X is Check/Do Action. All hotkeys can be reassigned in Options. The Controls page does not name a crop next to either button.
claims.versionCondition: Controls page oldid 192481.
claims.publicQuote: Use tool or place item
claims.limit: Do not assign either button to a Parsnip. See F22.

claims.statement: Xbox overworld: A is Check / Do Action / Use Cursor, and X is Use Tool. The page says controller buttons cannot be reassigned.
claims.versionCondition: Controls page. The table header is Xbox One / Xbox 360 Controller.
claims.publicQuote: Controller buttons can not be reassigned.
claims.limit: These labels are not a statement that A or X picks a Parsnip.

claims.statement: PlayStation overworld: Cross is Check / Do Action / Use Cursor, and Square is Use Tool. Buttons can be reassigned systemwide in Settings, Accessibility, Button Assignments.
claims.versionCondition: Controls page.
claims.publicQuote: Check / Do Action / Use Cursor
claims.limit: Same limit as F17. Do not treat a system remap as the game's harvest instruction.

claims.statement: Switch overworld: A is Check / Do Action / Use Cursor, and Y is Use Tool. Buttons can be reassigned systemwide under System Settings, Controllers and Sensors, Change Button Mapping. A later Weapons section says Y is basic attack and A is block or alternate attack. That weapons pair is not the overworld tool pair.
claims.versionCondition: Controls page.
claims.publicQuote: Use Tool
claims.limit: Do not merge the Weapons section into crop harvesting.

claims.statement: Switch 2 mouse controls, when enabled, use R to pick up furniture or use a tool, and ZR to rotate furniture, interact with the environment, or use other items. R Stick scrolls the toolbar. Mouse controls can be turned off in Options.
claims.versionCondition: Controls page section Nintendo Switch 2 Mouse Controls.
claims.publicQuote: The R button to pick up furniture or use a tool
claims.limit: The page does not say R or ZR picks a crop.

claims.statement: Mobile's default scheme is Tap-to-move and Auto-Attack. Tapping stones or wood auto-selects the tool, and the stated exception is the scythe, which must be selected. Other schemes map Button A to perform action, called right-click on PC, and Button X to use tool, called left-click on PC. None of those scheme descriptions says a crop uses Button A or Button X.
claims.versionCondition: Mobile Controls oldid 189843, revision timestamp 2025-12-05 from the wiki API.
claims.publicQuote: The one exception with tools is the scythe, which must be selected to use.
claims.limit: Do not pick one mobile scheme as the only way to harvest. Do not infer the crop button from the PC mapping.

claims.statement: The opened wiki pages do not name the button that picks a Parsnip. Parsnip has growth text and no tool sentence. Getting Started does not name a harvest button. Controls defines the buttons without naming a crop. Mobile names the scythe exception without naming the crop button. PC right-click is named only in the player posts in F43 and F44.
claims.versionCondition: Pages read 2026-10-12: Parsnip oldid 191123, Getting Started oldid 195315, Controls oldid 192481, Mobile Controls oldid 189843.
claims.limit: The wiki absence stays. Do not fill it from the AI Overview or an unwatched video. The player-post mapping is F43 and F44, not a wiki sentence.

claims.statement: The Crops page says seeds and fertilizer are placed with the left-click control, or across tiles by holding right-click or left-click. It says planting and fertilizing require no tool and use no energy. That paragraph is about planting and fertilizing, not about harvesting.
claims.versionCondition: Crops page oldid 193979, API timestamp 2026-08-13.
claims.editorExcerpt: Seeds and fertilizer are placed on a tilled tile individually by using the left-click control
claims.limit: Do not reuse this left-click sentence as the harvest instruction.

claims.statement: Controls history for 1.4 says holding a button makes it easier to harvest large numbers of kegs, preserves jars, and crystalariums. The objects named are machines, not field crops.
claims.versionCondition: 1.4 history line on the Controls page.
claims.editorExcerpt: This makes harvesting large numbers of kegs/preserves jars/crystalariums, etc. easier by holding the button without releasing it.
claims.limit: Do not apply this hold-to-harvest line to a row of crops.

claims.statement: Crops are seasonal. After the 28th day, a crop that is no longer in season withers and dies. The named multi-season exceptions are Ancient Fruit, Coffee Bean, Corn, Sunflower, and Wheat. On the 1st, crops no longer in season leave a dead crop and the soil stays tilled. A multi-season crop that is still in season continues. Fully grown crops that are ready to harvest still wither when moving to a season they cannot occupy.
claims.versionCondition: Current Crops page. Greenhouse and Ginger Island persistence is F31, not this outdoor rule.
claims.publicQuote: Fully grown crops that are ready to harvest will wither and die when moving to a new season, however.
claims.limit: Giant crops are a further exception in F27. Do not use the 2021 Steam thread's numbers.

claims.statement: Dead crops left at the start of a season can be removed with a scythe. Removing them is not the same action as harvesting a ready crop.
claims.versionCondition: Current Crops page, End of Season.
claims.publicQuote: Dead crops can be removed with a scythe.
claims.limit: The page does not say a basic scythe destroys a living Parsnip.

claims.statement: Cauliflower, Melon, Pumpkin, Powdermelon, and Qi Fruit in a 3x3 can become a giant crop. Giants drop 15 to 21 normal-quality items when harvested with any axe, in three hits. The current condition is that the top-left crop is fully grown and watered. They do not die at a season change. They cannot grow in the greenhouse, in Garden Pots, or on Ginger Island. Junimos cannot harvest them.
claims.versionCondition: Current Crops page. A 2021 Steam reply quoted an older center-crop condition and 17-22 items. Those older figures are not this page.
claims.publicQuote: Giant crops drop 15–21 normal-quality items when harvested with any axe, taking three hits.
claims.limit: Junimo inability is on https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Junimo_Hut oldid 194144. Greenhouse inability is also on the Greenhouse page.

claims.statement: Green Bean, Hops, and Grape need a trellis. A trellis cannot be walked through until the crop is dead, so the layout has to leave the crop reachable. Junimos can pass through trellis tiles.
claims.versionCondition: Current Crops page. Junimo passage is on the Junimo Hut page.
claims.publicQuote: Some crops require a trellis, which cannot be walked through
claims.limit: Green Bean regrowth is F30. This claim is only about reaching the plant.

claims.statement: Grow times on the Crops page, and in the game according to that page, exclude the day the seeds were planted. A 5-day crop planted on day 1 is ready on day 6. Parsnip's own page lists growth time of 4 days and stage days totaling 4. Getting Started says parsnips are ready to harvest in 4 days. Applying the Crops counting rule to that 4-day listing is an application of the Crops page, not a calendar sentence printed on the Parsnip page.
claims.versionCondition: Crops oldid 193979. Parsnip oldid 191123. Getting Started oldid 195315.
claims.publicQuote: a 5-day crop will be ready for harvest on day 6, not day 5.
claims.limit: Unwatered days do not advance growth. That watering rule is on the same Crops section. Do not turn it into a watering guide.

claims.statement: Two opened examples continue after maturity. Green Bean uses a trellis and has regrowth of 3 days. Strawberry gives 1 strawberry every 4 days, and its table lists regrowth of 4 days. Coffee's visible sentence says the crop continues to produce after maturity. A coffee regrowth day count was not captured from the visible table, so none is stated.
claims.versionCondition: Examples read on the Crops page. Not a census of every regrowing crop.
claims.publicQuote: This crop uses a trellis, and continues to produce after maturity.
claims.limit: The quoted sentence is the Green Bean line. Strawberry's every-4-days sentence is a second line on the same page.

claims.statement: After the Greenhouse is repaired, crops there can be planted, grown, and harvested at any time of year. They still need water, including on rainy days. Crops that regrow do not die at the end of a season. Giant crops cannot grow there. Multiple-harvest crops and fertilizer do not disappear unless the player removes them. The page says that fertilizer persistence is also true on Ginger Island.
claims.versionCondition: Current Greenhouse page. Repair method is on the page and is not the harvest action.
claims.publicQuote: Crops can be planted, grown, and harvested at any time of year
claims.limit: The profitability list on this page is a different intent. Do not import it.

claims.statement: A Junimo Hut's Junimos harvest mature crops in range, including flowers, tea leaves, scythe crops including fiber, and trellis crops. They can pass through trellis. The player gains no Farming XP from those harvests. Quality still uses the player's Farming level. They do not work in winter or rain, and they do not collect wild-seed forage, Garden Pots, trees, or giant crops. The bag holds 36 items. Further harvested crops drop on the ground when it is full.
claims.versionCondition: Current Junimo Hut page. The 17 by 17 range is on the page and is secondary to the harvest action.
claims.publicQuote: Junimos will harvest crops around the hut for you.
claims.limit: The 36-item overflow is the Junimo bag, not the player's backpack. Build cost and quest prerequisites are not the how-to.

claims.statement: The Mastery Cave unlocks after level 10 in all five skills. Mastery points accumulate only after that, and Farming experience counts at 50 percent. Experience from before 1.6 does not carry over. The player chooses the order. Claim costs by order are 10000, 15000, 20000, 25000, and 30000 points. Farming Mastery's listed rewards are the Iridium Scythe and the Statue of Blessings recipe.
claims.versionCondition: Mastery exists from 1.6. The cave page says pre-1.6 excess experience does not carry over. Oldid 191046 from the wiki API.
claims.publicQuote: It is unlocked after the player has achieved level 10 in all 5 skills.
claims.limit: Do not write that Farming level 10 alone unlocks the Iridium Scythe. Do not assign one point cost to Farming Mastery.

claims.statement: Getting Started says Farming XP is earned by harvesting a fully grown crop and by taking care of animals. It also says the default control for eating food is right-click or X, and that talking to a villager is right-click. Those two button sentences are not crop-harvest sentences.
claims.versionCondition: Getting Started oldid 195315, API timestamp 2026-10-09.
claims.publicQuote: Farming XP is earned by harvesting a fully grown crop and taking care of animals.
claims.limit: Adjacent only. The site already has a farming-XP article. Do not expand this keyword into that guide. Do not move the eating or talking button onto crops.

claims.statement: The live URL https://stardewvalleyplanner.art/how-to-harvest-stardew-valley returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-12. The English slug list in src/blog/blog-post-identities.ts has no harvest slug.
claims.versionCondition: Live response and the current worktree source read the same day.
claims.limit: A 404 means this slug is not a published harvest guide. It does not describe the game.

claims.statement: The planner homepage says the tool lets a player choose from 8 farm types, place buildings and crops, switch seasons, check coverage, and import saves. The live homepage HTML, 95344 bytes, contained that sentence and contained no occurrence of harvest or scythe. A source search of src/planner for harvest or scythe found no matches.
claims.versionCondition: Live homepage and src/homepage/homepage-copy.ts line 170, plus a src/planner text search, all on 2026-10-12.
claims.publicQuote: place buildings and crops, switch seasons, check coverage, and import saves.
claims.limit: The tool does not perform the harvest action. Do not add a harvest call to action.

claims.statement: The English array in src/blog/blog-post-registry.tsx currently ends with three titles: What to Grow in Greenhouse Stardew: Choose by Access, Harvest Rhythm, and Replanting; Stardew Fruit: Find Its Source Before Buying Seeds; Stardew Valley Oak Tree vs Maple: The Seed or the Tapper Product Names the Tree. Registry history shows the fruit commit on 2026-09-26 and the greenhouse commit on 2026-09-26. The newest commit touching that registry file is 6482925 on 2026-09-27.
claims.versionCondition: Source registry in this worktree. Live checks: greenhouse, fruit, and oak URLs returned HTTP 200.
claims.limit: These titles are neighboring articles. Their bodies were not used as harvest facts. 6482925 was dated from git log of the registry file, not opened as an article.

claims.statement: Live llms.txt returned HTTP 200 and 12308 bytes. It contains the English greenhouse and oak-versus-maple URLs, and the farming-XP and last-day-to-plant URLs. It does not contain how-to-harvest or stardew-fruit. The fruit URL itself still returned HTTP 200, so the llms file is an incomplete index.
claims.versionCondition: Full file searched on 2026-10-12.
claims.limit: A missing llms line is not a missing page, as the fruit URL shows.

claims.statement: One Google sample for the exact query was taken in ego-browser on 2026-10-12 at 14:08:07Z. Details, including the United States footer label, the result list, and the pages not opened, are in serp-evidence.json. That file is one sample, not a stable US top ranking.
claims.versionCondition: Sample time 2026-10-12T14:08:07Z. hl=en and gl=us were requested. The footer said results were not personalized and United States from the IP. That is still one session.
claims.limit: Do not cite the AI Overview, the Reddit snippet, or the YouTube snippets as game rules.

claims.statement: The Farming page says experience comes from harvesting crops, and that more expensive crops give more experience. Its 1.3.27 history line says a bug that blocked Farming XP when harvesting with a Scythe was fixed. The page does not name a mouse or controller button for picking a crop.
claims.versionCondition: Farming page oldid 191914. The 1.3.27 line is a bugfix, not a current XP table for scythe crops.
claims.publicQuote: Fixed bug that prevented farming XP being granted when harvesting with Scythe.
claims.limit: Adjacent to the button gap. Do not expand it into the existing farming-XP article, and do not treat the scythe XP bugfix as the harvest button.

claims.statement: On 2026-10-12 the English wiki text search API returned totalhits 0 for the query Check/Do Action plus crop. Searches that included right-click or left-click plus harvest matched planting on the Crops page, eating on Getting Started, animal menus, or unrelated pages. None of the returned snippets was a sentence that picks an ordinary crop with Check/Do Action or Use tool.
claims.versionCondition: MediaWiki search API, srwhat=text, five queries, limit 5. A search miss is not proof the sentence exists nowhere.
claims.limit: Do not convert a nearby Right Click on the eating paragraph into a crop action.

claims.statement: On the official Stardew Valley forum thread PC controls vs mobile, started September 17, 2021, player Elenna101 wrote that holding right click harvests and plants on the tile the character is standing on, and that X is automatically mapped to right click. The fetched reply has no separate timestamp. A later reply in the thread treats the mobile 1.5 hold control as not yet available. This is a player post, not a ConcernedApe post and not the wiki.
claims.versionCondition: Thread start date September 17, 2021. Not a 1.6.15 patch note. The reply was re-read on the live thread on 2026-10-12.
claims.publicQuote: If you hold right click with the mouse not near your character, you'll automatically plant seed and harvest on the tile you're standing on
claims.editorExcerpt: X is automatically mapped to right click
claims.limit: Use this as the positive PC gesture the player described. Do not add a claim that left-click cannot harvest. Do not treat the post as console or mobile instructions.

claims.statement: The Steam thread Harvest Parsnip with Scythe?? was started March 25, 2019. The March 26, 2019, 5:01am reply, shown under the Automaton Spy profile and quoted by the next reply as Kzar, says a parsnip does not need the scythe and is harvested by standing next to it and right-clicking. The same reply also says amaranth or wheat need a scythe and that any other crop is right-clicked. That any-other-crop sentence is not adopted.
claims.versionCondition: Player replies from March 2019, before the 1.6 Iridium Scythe. Not a current patch note.
claims.publicQuote: You don't NEED the scythe for parsnips.
claims.editorExcerpt: you need to be standing next to it and rightclick it
claims.limit: The 2019 any-other-crop wording is not a 1.6.15 rule. The current wiki also names Kale, Unmilled Rice, and Fiber Seeds as scythe harvests. The next reply in this thread already names Kale as the spring scythe crop. Do not copy the any-other-crop clause forward.

claims.statement: The PC inputs named for harvesting in F43 are right click and X. A re-read of Controls on 2026-10-12 still lists X on the Check/Do Action row, and the earlier full read of oldid 192481 lists right-click or X as Check/Do Action. The wiki row names the buttons. It still does not say they harvest a crop. The harvest mapping comes from F43 and F44.
claims.versionCondition: Controls oldid 192481, re-read 2026-10-12 for the X and Check/Do Action row.
claims.publicQuote: Check/Do Action
claims.limit: Do not extend this PC pairing to Xbox A, PlayStation Cross, Switch A, or a mobile tap. Those buttons share a wiki label, not these player sentences.

claims.statement: A filename search under the V7 workflow folder and this worktree, depth 3, for a content-pack, content-factory, or official-content file returned no paths.
claims.versionCondition: Search only. No pack was opened because none was found.
claims.limit: Record is 无. This does not prove a pack exists somewhere outside those two folders.

candidateIntents.intent: How to harvest a crop: which opened crops require a scythe, what the Iridium Scythe adds for ordinary crops, and which documented button is Use tool versus Check/Do Action on PC, Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, Switch 2 mouse, and mobile.
candidateIntents.mustNotInvent: A console or mobile crop button, a ban on left-click, or the 2019 any-other-crop wording. PC right-click is F43 and F44.

candidateIntents.intent: What happens if a ready outdoor crop is not harvested: it withers when the season changes, with the named multi-season, Wheat Fall 1, Greenhouse, and Ginger Island exceptions.
candidateIntents.source: People Also Ask in serp-evidence.json, answered only from F12, F25, and F31.

candidateIntents.intent: How to tell a crop is ready: the listed growth time, counted as nights under F29. A green plus cursor was not on the wiki pages read.
candidateIntents.source: People Also Ask in serp-evidence.json. The plus-sign wording stays a snippet, not a fact.

candidateIntents.intent: A documented later way for mature crops is the Junimo Hut in F32. Holding right click while walking is a 2021 player report in F43, not a wiki rule.
candidateIntents.source: People Also Ask asked for a faster way. F32 is the wiki answer. F43 is the player-reported PC gesture.

candidateIntents.intent: Giant crops are harvested with an axe, not the scythe or the ordinary pick. F27.
Trellis crops have to stay reachable because the player cannot walk through them. F28.

separateIntents: How to level Farming, beyond the single Getting Started sentence in F34.
What to grow, gold per day, or a crop ranking.
The 2021 official-forum suggestion for new harvest tools.

gaps.statement: Wiki pages still do not name the Parsnip button. PC right-click is named by the 2021 official-forum player post and the 2019 Steam parsnip reply. Console and mobile crop buttons are still unnamed.
gaps.blockingFor: Assigning Xbox A, PlayStation Cross, Switch A, or a mobile tap to a crop, and any sentence that says left-click cannot harvest.
gaps.notAConflict: The wiki does not contradict the player posts. It does not say the sentence. The AI Overview's left-click line stays unused.

gaps.statement: No opened page says whether a basic or Golden Scythe destroys a living non-scythe crop.
gaps.blockingFor: Any destroy or safe-to-swing claim about Parsnips.

gaps.statement: No opened page says the player's full backpack blocks a crop harvest. The 36-item drop is only the Junimo bag.
No opened page says a hand harvest spends energy. Holding right click to plant and harvest while walking is the 2021 player sentence in F43, not a wiki rule.
gaps.blockingFor: An energy-cost claim, and any wording that promotes F43 from a player post to a wiki rule.

excluded: Green plus or plus-sign cursor. Seen in Google and YouTube snippets, not on the wiki pages read.
Reddit post body. The old.reddit page title loaded, the body was not extracted, and a later JSON request returned HTTP 403.
Facebook results at SERP positions 3 and 7. Not opened.
2021 Steam giant-crop figures of a center crop and 17-22 items.
Gold-per-day tables and the Greenhouse profitability list.
A complete regrowth census, and a coffee regrowth day count.
A claim that the scythe-crop list is exhaustive.
Player backpack capacity and upgrade prices. The Inventory page was not re-read in this settlement.
The original 1.6 launch changelog. Iridium introduction rests on the tool page history.
